title: Pay dispute at the Savoy and leaving Webb
summary: He pushes for better pay, clashes with Savoy management, gives notice and Webb cries; he moves to Don Redman.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Chick getting big, big. So naturally, I want to see the money too, and I know about (inaudible) already making money for that band, and they don't want to pay the guys, not so much. So I begin to speak. So we came at the manager, the Savoy, the next day. He says, oh, you --

That's Charlie Buchanan. He was (inaudible), and Mo Gale was the owner of the ballroom and the manager of Chick Webb, and they (inaudible). Oh, you're trying to create a revolution here. You're Latino. You're Franco. You're dictators. I say, no, I'm not a dictator. I think we deserve money. You get money for the band. How you know? I say, well, listen. I thought a deal was going on, you know.

So the guy's so bad, went to the Paramount Theater, I said this is it. So Chick called me, said, Mario, I've got to give you your notice. I said, all right. Well, gave my two week notice. So the day I'm supposed to leave he come into the dressing room. He start crying, don't want me to leave.

I say no. I'm a man of principle. I won't play another hour in this band. Maybe less money next year. You leave, I play for you now. Principle, I gotta leave. That's all there is to it. I know -- I say, I know what all the
So every night he used to come and look for me around my house, spend all kind of hours talking about this and that, everything. So I went with Don Redmon. I started with Don -- (Side 2.)
